svg.title: Britain’s Industrial Revolution: Coalfields, Steam, Cotton & Iron (1750–1830)
svg.desc: KS3 Year 8 historical GIS atlas map of Great Britain (England, Wales, and Scotland) and unpartitioned Ireland showing major land-clipped coalfields, Coalbrookdale coke iron smelting, Boulton and Watt’s Soho steam manufactory in Birmingham, Manchester’s Cottonopolis mills and Liverpool port, paired with a zoomed Hampshire and Solent GIS inset of Henry Cort’s Funtley Ironworks and the 1787 Portsmouth Royal Dockyard Admiralty trials.

svg.text: KS3 HISTORY • YEAR 8 ENQUIRY: INDUSTRIALISATION & REFORM (1750–1872)
Britain’s Industrial Revolution: Coalfields, Steam, Cotton & Iron (1750–1830)
Abundant coal and Boulton & Watt’s rotary steam engines freed British mills from river valleys, turning Manchester into “Cottonopolis”.
In Hampshire, Henry Cort’s Funtley puddling furnace and 1787 Portsmouth Dockyard trials gave Britain world-leading wrought iron.
